title: India monsoon 2025 with NASA rain anomaly frames

link.method: Pearson r, monthly means 2023-01 to 2025-09 (33 months): all-India land rain (IMERG Final monthly, observed) vs India land NDVI (MODIS MOD13C2), NDVI lagging by 0 to 3 months; best positive lag reported
link.lag_days_note: lag_steps = lag in months x 30.44 days (monthly resolution, so +/- about 15 days)

gaps: EIC layer: NASA SVS item 4897 frames show the IMERG precipitation anomaly, the departure from IMERG's own climatology, in mm/day. Each day's departure is added and then fades over about three months, so a frame is a slowly fading memory of recent weeks, not the rain of that day; it lags the daily rain lane. The climatology period is not stated on the item page.

EIC colours are 8 flat bins of the item's colour bar: -2 to -5, -5 to -10, -10 to -15, beyond -15 (drier) and 2 to 5, 5 to 10, 10 to 15, beyond 15 mm/day (wetter). Within -2 to +2 mm/day the frame is transparent: read as normal (0). A pixel's value is its bin mid value (3.5, 7.5, 12.5, 17.5), so values are steps of a binned map, not measurements.
Harmony tension in this story = |EIC anomaly| at the listening point divided by 17.5 mm/day (bin mid value), clamped to 1; wetter and drier count the same; 0 inside the transparent near-normal band.

EIC frames on the globe: 62 of 365 daily frames (every 3rd day June to October, the 1st of every other month, and 31 December), each held until the next; shown at 2048 x 1024, nearest-neighbour from 3600 x 1800, so colours are exact. The EIC lane uses all daily frames.

EIC lane: India land mean of the binned anomaly (0.1 deg frame pixels averaged to 0.5 deg cells inside India, cosine latitude weighted). Because near-normal pixels count as 0 and wet and dry bins cancel, the lane is a rough summary of the map, not an IMERG computation.

Rain is IMERG Late Run v07 (GPM_3IMERGDL): satellite estimates with a climatological gauge adjustment, available within about a day. The Final Run with monthly gauge calibration (used for the 2019 story) ends on 30 September 2025, so the Late Run is used for all of 2025 to keep one product. Daily values over mountains carry larger errors.
Onset here is a data rule on the all-India land mean (7-day mean rain at or above 5 mm/day for 15 days in a row), not the India Meteorological Department onset over Kerala.
Rain map frames are 8-day means at 0.5 deg (46 frames, the last covers 5 days); the colour scale is linear 0 to 40 mm/day with a floor of 1 mm/day (99.5th percentile of the frames: 41.8 mm/day).

Wind is MERRA-2 reanalysis (a model) at 850 hPa, about 1.5 km up, daily means drawn as 7-day means at 1 x 1.25 deg; the lane is the Arabian Sea box 10 to 20 N, 65 to 72.5 E. Where the ground is above 850 hPa (Tibetan Plateau, high Himalaya) cells are empty.
NDVI is a monthly MODIS composite: the lane holds each month's value on every day of that month (a step, not interpolated).
India means use 0.5 deg cells whose centre falls inside the Natural Earth 1:50m outline of India (cosine latitude weighted).

The rain to NDVI link uses monthly means 2023-01 to 2025-09 (33 months, IMERG Final monthly ends 2025-09). Both follow the seasonal cycle, so the correlation mostly says that vegetation greens after the rains. Lag resolution is one month.

GRACE-FO water thickness is shown on a 0.5 deg grid but its real resolution is about 300 km; it measures total water change relative to a 2004 to 2009 mean, not rain. Water map: linear -40 to 40 cm, no floor.
Water lane: 13 days of 2025 fall outside GRACE-FO solution date ranges and stay empty (not bridged).
Link strength: rain to NDVI r 0.854 (strong) at 2 month lag, n 31; rain to GRACE water r 0.892 (strong) at 2 month lag, n 31.

hero_norm.method: min..max of the hero series itself (all-India land mean daily rain, IMERG Late, 2025)
